title: Event-Driven Payment Reconciliation Engine with Double-Entry Ledger
problem: Financial platforms process millions of money movements across payment gateways, banking settlement rails, and merchant accounts. Webhook packet loss, bank batch file settlement delays, currency rounding, and timezone drift cause constant transaction discrepancies. Manual reconciliation is slow and prone to errors. This project builds an automated, event-driven payment reconciliation engine in Python and FastAPI. The system processes payment gateway webhook streams from Kafka, parses daily bank settlement CSV files, enforces double-entry ledger accounting invariants in PostgreSQL, executes three-way match algorithms across transactions, classifies breaks into distinct categories (unmatched settlement, fee drift, timing discrepancy), and generates audit-ready financial break reports.
use_cases: FinTech payment processor daily settlement reconciliation against banking partner clearing files
E-commerce merchant multi-gateway audit verifying Stripe, Adyen, and PayPal payout accuracy
Lending platform loan disbursement and repayment tracking with automated discrepancy detection
hard_parts: Enforcing immutable double-entry ledger accounting invariants (Assets = Liabilities + Equity) across high concurrency
Resolving three-way matching between asynchronous gateway webhooks, internal ledger entries, and delayed bank clearing files
Classifying financial discrepancies into actionable break buckets (unmatched settlement, fee mismatch, timing drift)
Ensuring idempotent event ingestion so replayed Kafka webhooks never create duplicate ledger journal postings
screener_signals: Clean Python implementation separating double-entry ledger, Kafka consumers, reconciliation matchers, and break reporters
Automated reconciliation test suite with 25 intentionally seeded financial break scenarios verifying 100% detection
Anti-fake verification script injecting a dynamic unrecorded settlement row and asserting exact discrepancy flag generation

components.name: Double-Entry General Ledger Core
components.purpose: Enforces immutable debit/credit journal entries and guarantees ledger balance invariant integrity

components.name: Kafka Webhook Ingestion Consumer
components.purpose: Consumes gateway payment webhooks idempotently, preventing duplicate transaction recordings

components.name: Bank Settlement File Parser
components.purpose: Parses structured daily bank clearing CSV/BAI2 settlement records and normalizes payout line items

components.name: Three-Way Reconciliation Matcher
components.purpose: Executes rule-based matching across gateway events, internal orders, and bank settlement deposits

components.name: Financial Break Classifier & Reporter
components.purpose: Categorizes unmatched records into fee, timing, and missing break buckets, exposing audit endpoints

architecture.data_flow: Payment gateway webhooks arrive via Kafka; the Ingestion Consumer validates idempotency and posts balanced debit/credit entries to the Double-Entry General Ledger; daily bank settlement CSV files are ingested by the Settlement Parser; the Three-Way Reconciliation Matcher links internal order IDs, gateway transaction references, and bank settlement lines; matching records are marked RECONCILED; mismatched records are categorized by the Break Classifier into fee variances, timing delays, or missing settlements; audit reports and summary metrics are exposed via FastAPI.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: PostgreSQL database check constraints guaranteeing zero debit/credit imbalance per journal transaction; idempotent event keys preventing double posting.

prerequisites: Proficiency in Python, SQL relational databases, and data manipulation libraries (Pandas)
Understanding of double-entry accounting fundamentals (debits, credits, trial balance) and event-driven patterns

environment.gpu: None required (purely CPU-bound data processing and SQL execution)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external cloud accounts, paid services, or API keys required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with Python 3.11 and PostgreSQL 15+ installed
environment.fallback_path: SQLite in-memory database with POSIX CSV file simulation if Docker/Kafka cannot be started

riskiest_component.name: Floating Point Rounding Errors Causing False Ledger Break Alerts
riskiest_component.fallback: Enforce integer minor currency units (cents/paise) or Python Decimal throughout all calculations

deliverables: Git repository containing Python reconciliation engine, double-entry ledger models, and FastAPI app
Deterministic financial discrepancy test generator injecting known break scenarios
Automated reconciliation audit harness outputting trial balance and break summaries
Screener verification script executing automated benchmark and dynamic break test in under 2 minutes
out_of_scope: Direct SWIFT MT101 / ISO 20022 inter-bank wire clearing integration
Automated banking credit underwriting and loan origination decisioning
Live physical cash vault counting and ATM network reconciliation
safety_note: This project processes synthetic financial records and mock transaction identifiers for educational testing. It does not interface with live banking payment rails, initiate real fund transfers, or process sensitive cardholder payment details.
resources: Martin Fowler: Accounting Patterns and Double-Entry Ledger Principles
Financial Data Reconciliation Architecture and Break Management Standards
FastAPI and PostgreSQL High-Performance Ledger Design Documentation

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: an automated event-driven payment reconciliation engine in Python with double-entry ledger, Kafka webhook consumer, and break classifier.
worksheet.q2: Target users: FinTech engineers, core banking platform developers, and financial data engineers.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: daily payment gateway settlement reconciliation, multi-gateway merchant audit, and lending repayment reconciliation.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 39 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 34 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 39.1 -> 39 hours. Advanced level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: double-entry ledger accounting invariants, three-way matching logic, financial break classification, and idempotent webhook ingestion.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 50,000 transactions, 48,000 settlement lines, and 25 seeded breaks. Synthetic records only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: SQLite in-memory mode.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: Floating-point currency rounding errors. Fallback: integer cents/paise or Python Decimal throughout.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: hardcoded break reports. Anti-fake check 5 injects dynamic deposit line at runtime and asserts UNMATCHED break flag.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; synthetic financial records only, no live banking rails or real funds.
